segments.he: עוד אמר איך שהספר הגנוז הוא גדול (כמובא בחיי' מזה באריכות שהוא עין לא ראתה ששום בריאה לא ידע אפי' דבר שם רק משיח יאמר עליו פירוש וכו') והספר הנשרף גדול. אבל הר"ה שלי הוא עוד יותר גדול (כמו שאמר שאין דבר גדול מזה "קיין גרעסערס דער פין איז ניטא") "וויא דער ספר הגנוז איז גרוס דער ספר הנשרף איז מיין ר"ה נאך גרעסיר" (היינו להיות אצלו על ר"ה): עוד אמר אלמלא הר"ה שלו הי' העולם נעשה תוהו ובוהו "ווען מט מיין ר"ה וואלט דיא וועלט גווארין תוהו ובוהו".
segments.en:
Reb Yudel — when he drew close to Rabbainu (and several stories are cited in Kokhav Or) — he was already old and greatly famous in the world, a distinguished disciple of the holy Tzaddik Reb Pinchas of Koritz. Rabbainu would call him just "Yudel" — without the title "Reb" — as he called his other disciples. This distressed Reb Yudel. When Rabbainu saw it upset him, he called him "Reb Yudel." But afterward, once Reb Yudel understood Rabbainu's greatness, he very much wanted Rabbainu to call him simply "Yudel" — as Rabbainu called Reb Noson. But Rabbainu did not want to.

This Reb Yudel was the son-in-law of the holy Reb Leib Trestizer, one of the great disciples of the Ba'al Shem Tov. He ate kest at his home. Once a pot of plain food was before them and Reb Yudel could not eat it. Reb Leib turned his own plate so that the side facing him was now facing Reb Yudel — and immediately Reb Yudel felt in that same food all the finest tastes in the world.

When Reb Leib traveled to the Holy Land, a sea creature appeared and wanted to overturn the ship. Reb Leib went out to face it wrapped in tallis and tefillin — and it immediately returned to the sea. And Reb Leib passed away on the ship. He said: if not for his son-in-law Reb Yudel being with him, he would not have let him die on the ship. He commanded that he be tied to a plank alongside the ship — and wherever the ship came to rest, he should be buried there. When they came to Izmir the ship stopped, and they understood he was to be buried there. And the author of the Ba'al Shem Mussar — when he passed away — left a will that no one should be placed beside him until an Ashkenazic sage from Poland came, and when a pillar of fire appeared at the newcomer, he should be placed beside him. And so it was — and they placed Reb Leib beside him. And this Reb Leib came to Rabbainu after his death and requested that Rabbainu draw close Reb Yudel and his family. And so it was — they all drew close to Rabbainu.
